sections.title: Abstract
sections.prose: We test a new source-only data-selection policy for Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. Two source-trained LoRA probes estimate opposite-fold response-loss reduction. A quota-constrained selector combines structural complete-trace eligibility, positive transfer-gain leaders, and topic/length coverage, then trains a fresh full-parameter model on 15,000 unchanged original pairs. A fresh random control samples the broader prepared source pool and uses the same training cutoff and optimizer recipe. Comparative findings remain pending.

sections.title: Task and comparison scope
sections.prose: The assignment asks for an original-model baseline, reasoning SFT on a random 15K subset of the supplied 100K source, an advanced 15K selection, evaluation, analysis, code, models, and datasets. This experiment samples its random control uniformly from the broad prepared source pool after deduplication, benchmark/source-heldout exclusions, prompt-capacity bounds, and reserved-probe exclusions. It does not apply the advanced complete-short-trace, boxed-answer, repetition, topic, or gain criteria to random sampling. This is a random subset after declared preparation, not literal uniform sampling over the untouched original 100K. Keep that distinction explicit without assuming the instructor accepts any particular interpretation.

sections.title: Source data and exclusions
sections.prose: Use only the pinned redsgnaoh/acereason11_100k source and preserve original question/response pairs in dataset exports. Canonicalize and deduplicate prompt identities, reserve 1,000 source-only held-out questions before selection, and remove lexical matches to benchmark questions and held-out prompts. A shared prompt-capacity bound reserves room for supervised response tokens. Benchmark answers and measured benchmark outcomes do not enter selection. Supplementary AIME25 question exclusions occur before GPU probe training. Both final arms exclude all held-out questions and both reserved probe sets. Record the broad random population separately from the advanced complete-trace population and scoring reservoir.

sections.title: Cross-fitted transfer gain and coverage
sections.prose: Split source prompt identities into deterministic folds. Train one rank-eight LoRA probe on 512 complete originals from each fold for 64 updates. Score each frozen reservoir candidate with the original model and the probe trained on its opposite fold. The score is normalized response-loss reduction, (CE_base - CE_opposite_probe) / max(CE_base, 1e-8). Topic clusters and response-length cells determine capped quotas. At most half each cell is filled with positive-gain leaders; seeded coverage fills the remainder. The final selected model initializes from the original base, never from a probe. This is an experimental synthesis, with no established global-novelty or superiority claim.

sections.title: Advanced eligibility and broad random control
sections.prose: Advanced candidates must preserve complete source targets within the 8,192-token training cutoff and a 32-token selection margin, have at least 128 response tokens, a complete final boxed answer, limited repeated eight-grams, and balanced ordered think tags. These are structural checks, not independent mathematical correctness verification. Advanced selection uses a frozen coverage-balanced scoring reservoir of at most 30,000 candidates. The random control samples the broader prepared source population without those complete-target quality filters. Both arms use the same 8K cutoff and preserve unchanged original dataset exports. Overlength random training sequences use declared prefixes without adding an invented EOS; record truncated-row and missing-supervised-EOS counts. Advanced targets may not truncate, and neither arm may silently drop selected rows.

sections.title: Matched full-parameter SFT
sections.prose: Both final arms use the same original base, system message, response-mask construction, one pass, 1,875 optimizer updates, and effective batch eight. Parameters and AdamW moments remain FP32; forward computation uses BF16 autocast. Each sequence contributes its mean shifted supervised-token cross entropy, then examples are averaged within an optimizer update. Deterministic samplers and consumption receipts verify one presentation of every unique selected row. Advanced caches preserve complete original targets and native end markers; random caches may contain explicitly reported 8K prefixes. Native Transformers Trainer is used for runtime compatibility; the framework choice is documented rather than described as a LLaMA-Factory run.

sections.title: Fixed evaluation and metrics
sections.prose: Evaluate the original, prepared-source random, and advanced models with the same benchmark contents, grader, prompt, runtime, hardware settings, and eight-sample generation protocol. Report per-question mean sample correctness as pass@1 and any-of-eight correctness as pass@8. Retain repeated benchmark records with distinct identities; paired uncertainty should resample duplicate-question clusters together. Report the supplied eight-benchmark macro separately from the supplementary historical-seven internal macro. Historical runtime/dataset equivalence is unverified, so the latter is not an official leaderboard rank. Parse the actual MATH JSONL file as 500 records; its 499 newline characters explain the stale README table value.

sections.title: Results
sections.prose: Populate the tables only from complete, identity-checked evaluation artifacts. Leave missing values null and label partial coverage. A queued job, a completed training run, or a successful unit test does not establish benchmark accuracy.

sections.title: Analysis and limitations
sections.prose: Assess both accuracy and generation behavior. A pass@8 gain accompanied by a pass@1 or termination regression is a tradeoff. The current comparison tests the whole advanced policy: structural complete-target filtering, scoring-reservoir construction, transfer scoring, and coverage allocation. Complete-target eligibility also changes length distribution and EOS survival relative to broad random training prefixes. A separate eligible-random arm and a coverage-only arm using the same reservoir and quotas are needed to isolate those contributions; neither is currently part of the planned model pair. Lexical decontamination cannot rule out semantic contamination. Teacher-forced loss reduction is not proof of trace correctness or causal learning utility. One training seed and small benchmarks limit statistical precision.

sections.title: Reproducibility and deliverables
sections.prose: Provide exact model/source revisions, source and dataset hashes, selected prompt identities, source-only reservations, actual probe/score manifests, cache masks, training recipes, finite-state receipts, benchmark identities, and raw evaluation artifacts where feasible. Publish the required models and datasets with usable cards and verified links, provide the final repository README, and prepare the final report for team submission. No publication or course submission is established by this draft.

limitations: Relative teacher-forced loss reduction is a proxy, not verified mathematical correctness or causal data utility.
Random sampling is uniform within the broad prepared source pool after declared shared exclusions, not untouched original100K.
Random targets may be truncated by the shared 8K training cutoff, while complete-target fit is part of advanced selection; report this rate and do not attribute all gains to transfer scoring.
Separate eligible-random and coverage-only ablations would be needed to isolate transfer gain from eligibility and coverage allocation.
No novelty or state-of-the-art claim is established before results.
